The following sections of this walkthrough are grouped by section of the proposal form.
Select the applicable changes in the checkboxes/radio buttons.

Complete the following fields with your contact information.
Proposer Name Your name is automatically populated based on your Kuali account.
Proposer Title Enter your university role.
Proposer Email Enter your URI email address. This is the email reviewers will use if they have questions about your proposal.
Additional Proposer(s) Use this section to identify additional individuals who can speak to the proposed program.
Individuals listed here will not receive Kuali notifications or have access to edit the proposal. Their inclusion simply provides transparency to the reviewing committees about who else is involved in or can speak to the proposal.

Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the program to become effective. If the selected effective term has passed the applicable deadline by the time the proposal reaches the Faculty Senate, it will automatically be updated to the next available term.
First Graduation Term with Modifications Select the term and year in which you anticipate the students will graduate with the changes proposed.
Credential Type This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
Level This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
Academic Calendar This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
Important Information about Changing a Program’s Academic Calendar
If a program is currently offered on the Traditional Academic Calendar and you would like to move it to the Accelerated Academic Calendar, you cannot simply change the calendar while students are still enrolled in the program. The existing program must first be fully taught out. This requires a proposal to suspend admission to the program. Once there are no students remaining in the program, the program can be moved from one academic calendar to the other.

Alternatively, you may propose a new program by cloning the existing program. This approach does not require Board of Trustees approval and is treated as a program modification. Creating a separate program allows students to be appropriately coded according to the academic calendar in which their program is offered (Traditional or Accelerated).
Program Locations Select all locations where the program will be offered.
College This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you’ve selected Change Academic Home (department / college) from the Program Modification Section of the proposal.
Department This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you’ve selected Change Academic Home (department / college) from the Program Modification section of the proposal.
CIP Code This field will already be populated.
If it is not populated, enter the program’s current CIP Code as listed on eCampus.
If you are changing the program’s CIP code, make sure Change CIP Code is selected from the Program Modification section of the proposal, and enter the new code in the space provided.

Topics Course
Tags: courses
Short Description: A course that allows different topics to be offered under the same course number.
Topics Course
Topics courses allow different topics to be offered under the same course number.
8.81.20 Open-ended Course. An Open-ended Course shall be administered by the department which originated it. Initially, an open-ended course shall be proposed and approved in the same manner as other permanent courses (8.81.10). Prior to offering a specific topic the content of the course shall be approved in a department meeting.
8.81.21 After approval of each offering of an open-ended course topic, a copy of the title, subtitle, and description shall be forwarded for schedule authorization to the Office of Enrollment Services via the dean of the college in which the department resides. The dean’s authorization shall ensure that no overlap exists between specific topics and existing courses.

8.81.22 A specific topic within an open-ended course may be offered three times. After three offerings the topic shall be approved through the appropriate channels as either a permanent course or as a permanent topic within an open-ended course and shall be included in the University Catalog.
